text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, which helps other people work with it. One key idea is using clear naming conventions. For example, a variable called "userAge" is much better than "x". Functions should also be short and do only one job, so they are simple to test and reuse. When code is clean, it is easier to maintain. Fixing bugs or adding new features takes less time because the structure is clear. In short, writing clean code saves time and reduces mistakes for the whole team.
